teaser.en: The warm scent of a coast kitchen at breakfast, when *mahamri* are frying, comes largely from cardamom.

summary.en: Cardamom is an imported spice whose aromatic seed pods flavour many of the coast's best-loved foods. It goes into *mahamri*, *kashata*, *mkate wa kumimina* and spiced tea.

about.en: Cardamom comes from a tall, leafy plant of the ginger family. What reaches the kitchen are the small, pale green, three-sided pods, each holding a cluster of tiny dark, sticky seeds with a strong, sweet, slightly resinous scent.

where.en: Cardamom is not grown on the south coast; it is imported and bought in markets and shops.

uses.en: It flavours *mahamri*, the fried breakfast dough; *kashata*, the sweet of coconut, sugar and cardamom; and *mkate wa kumimina*, the poured rice-flour bread. It is also added to tea.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. Swahili calls it *iliki*. In English it is cardamom.

reason.en: Same family; ginger, another tea spice
Another imported spice for tea and rice
Coconut, the partner of cardamom in kashata

sources: Mwalonya, Nicolle, Nicolle & Zimbu, Mgombato: Digo-English-Swahili Dictionary (BTL / Digo Language and Literacy Project, 2004; e-version 2005)
